events.what: Chambers, 'On the square peg problem': inscribed squares for curves close to C2 in a stated sense
Greene and Lobb prove every Jordan curve formed by two graphs with Lipschitz constant below 1+sqrt(2) has an inscribed square, extending Tao 2017
Ueoka self-publishes (Zenodo, Medium) a claimed proof for all C0 Jordan curves, developed with Gemini and ChatGPT; the Zenodo page states an error was found
events.credibility_reason: Author's own notice on the Zenodo record: 'An error was found in this proof, so we are considering an alternative approach.'
events.ai_basis: AI systems used for English drafting, translation, structured proof-checking, and detecting missing links in arguments, with Ueoka selecting and validating the final structure and mathematical content.

judgement.doubts: Status, ai_role and direction already match the derivation (the 2026-09-28 corrections to partial/confirmed are right: a class of curves is settled, a case). credited_humans still named Ueoka, whose withdrawn claim no longer sets the status; replaced with the Greene-Lobb authors (surnames only, as the record gives them). ai.basis_quote describes the Ueoka episode, not the status event; left in place as evidence. The summary text still argues for `progress`/`incident`, which later corrections superseded. Chambers 2022 is pre-snapshot and its journal publication in 2025 is not a new event.

corrections.why: F8: the status rests on Greene and Lobb, 'Square pegs between two graphs' (arXiv:2407.07798), per the 2026-09-24 event correction; Ueoka's claim is knocked down by the author's own Zenodo notice ('An error was found in this proof') and cannot carry credit.
F8: the quote belongs to the discarded Ueoka event, not the Greene-Lobb event the status rests on; kept as evidence. Even for Ueoka it describes drafting and checking, which is `none` (F9).
